chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Abd al-Karim from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): In

a man who cursed his wife while she was pregnant, then claimed the child after she gave birth, asserting it was from him, so he said: 'The child is returned to him, and she becomes permissible for him, because the mutual cursing (li'an) has already taken place.'

key_terms.لاَعَنَ: li'an (mutual cursing between husband and wife to deny paternity)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a child born after li'an if the husband claims paternity?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies that the completion of the li'an ceremony (mutual cursing) severs the marital bond and attributes the child to the husband, even if paternity is claimed post-birth. It highlights the Shia juristic view that the ritual's finality overrides subsequent claims, ensuring the child's lineage is established while the wife becomes halal for him, reflecting the procedural rigor of the Quranic li'an mechanism.
